entities.summary: Ștefan Aurel Baciu was a Romanian and Brazilian poet, novelist, publicist and academic who lived his later life in Hawaii. A precocious, award-winning, young author in interwar Romania, he was involved in editing several literary magazines. Attracted into left-wing democratic politics and the Social Democratic Party (PSDR), he camouflaged his views while working for the fascist press under dictatorial regimes, but returned in 1944 to manage the PSDR's Libertatea newspaper. Witnessing first-hand the gradual communist takeover, Baciu managed to have himself assigned to a diplomatic posting in Switzerland, and ultimately defected in 1948.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a key figure in Romania's interwar literary scene and a prominent publicist for the Social Democratic Party (PSDR), Ștefan Baciu played a crucial role in shaping the country's politics during its transition from fascist to communist rule. His deflection in 1948 allowed him to escape the communist takeover, but his experiences during this period highlight the complexities of navigating political ideologies under authoritarian regimes.
